title: Awaken The Giant Within
author: Tony Robbins
blurb: Tony Robbins argues that the quality of your life comes down to a handful of things you can control: your decisions, your beliefs, and how you manage your emotions. He begins with the claim that a real decision, one that cuts off every other option, can change your direction in a moment. Then he explains the forces underneath our choices: we act to avoid pain and gain pleasure, and we can deliberately link new feelings to old habits. He shows how beliefs, the questions we habitually ask, and even the words we use to describe our experiences shape how we feel. He goes on to values and rules, the hidden compass behind every choice, and to identity, the deepest driver of all. The book closes with practical challenges for building lasting change through constant small improvement.

lessons.t: One Real Decision Can Change Everything
lessons.b: Your destiny is shaped in moments of decision, and a true decision means committing to a result and cutting off every other possibility.

lessons.t: Pain and Pleasure Run Your Life
lessons.b: Everything you do is driven by the need to avoid pain or gain pleasure, so lasting change comes from linking massive pain to the old habit and pleasure to the new one.
issues: scene 4: The cake slice drawing looks broken. The purple icing stroke overhangs the left edge of the slice, and the cherry and stem float off-centre above it, so the slice is hard to read as cake. (fix: Clip the icing stroke to the top edge of the slice's wedge shape. Seat the cherry on the icing at the slice's apex so the cake reads as one clean, intact object.)

lessons.b: Beliefs are feelings of certainty supported by past experiences, and you can weaken a limiting belief by questioning its references and strengthen an empowering one by adding new ones.
Thinking is largely asking and answering questions, so changing the questions you habitually ask changes what you focus on and how you feel.
issues: scene 5: Lec's running figure is malformed. The torso is a lumpy blob and the legs stick out at odd angles from the bottom, so it reads as a broken shape rather than a person running to freedom. (fix: Redraw Lec with the same head-and-shoulders silhouette used in scene 4. Add two clean angled leg strokes and a slight forward lean, attached under the torso, so the running pose is clear.)

lessons.t: Change Your Words, Change Your Feelings
lessons.b: The words you habitually use to label experiences intensify or soften your emotions, so deliberately choosing milder or stronger words changes your emotional state.

lessons.t: Values and Rules Steer Every Choice
lessons.b: Your ranked values and the rules you set for feeling them decide your choices and your happiness, so making your rules easier to meet lets you feel good more often.
